**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop local effects when the control channel disconnects**

If the WebSocket closes during TTS or a greeting, `main.ts` calls `disconnect()`, but this only quarantines the controller and clears its queue; it never invokes the local stop dependency. An already-started audio source therefore continues playing, and the MOD greeting can continue its remaining motion steps because its cancellation button was never pushed. Quarantine also disables the Cancel button and makes `cancel()` return null, leaving the operator unable to stop those effects through the page. Start local cancellation on disconnect while retaining quarantine regardless of the cleanup outcome.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject empty work IDs before constructing the core request**

After opening a scope, a `work` message with its valid token but an omitted or empty `id` passes `Message` validation because the envelope defaults `id` to an empty string. Constructing `Work` here then raises `ValidationError` because the core model requires `min_length=1`. That exception falls outside the validation handler and escapes the WebSocket route, triggering server-side cancellation and terminating the control connection instead of returning `rejected`. Validate the work-specific ID requirement inside the handled boundary so a malformed request cannot tear down an otherwise valid experiment session.
